extracted.intended_audience: readers and contributors of the Philosophical Transactions / early modern natural philosophers (astronomers, engineers, chemists, physicians, linguists)
extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic early-modern natural philosophy report describing conventions of Chinese writing, an engineering device to consume smoke, astronomical observations of Saturn's satellites and eclipses, chemical/hydrostatic reasoning, and a medical case with chemical analysis of calculi.

rubrics_metrics.name: Square-proportioned character grid
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Chinese character is allotted a certain square space proportioned to the intended writing size; no part of a character exceeds that square and characters occupy equal space in the line regardless of stroke count.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This regular square arrangement makes characters exactly ranged in rank and file (like arithmetical digits) and underlies printing/reproduction conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three general kinds of writing characters
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three principal kinds: (1) the fixed or set square form (most usual), (2) the running hand used for court orders (continuous pencil stroke, sometimes several characters without break), and (3) large flourishing letters used in titles, chapter-beginnings, epitaphs and inscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each kind is composed of the same strokes but modulated; the third is shaped to appear more beautiful and regular and is used for display inscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printed characters reproduce written stroke detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed Chinese characters express every variety of stroke, line, or point made with the pencil so exactly that printed forms match written hands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fidelity suggests printing is done more like copper cuts with a rolling-press rather than coarse wooden cuts; it explains the close correspondence between handwritten and printed forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper properties and one-sided printing / binding method
rubrics_metrics.description: Their paper is very thin, fine, transparent and brown; writing/printing is typically only on one side of a leaf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To appear double-sided they fold sheets with printed sides outwards and sew/stitch cut edges together; titles often set on a whole thicker leaf and sheet numbers written on the fold edge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading and book layout order
rubrics_metrics.description: Books begin at the top right-hand side and are read downward to the bottom; the next line begins at the top left and reads downward, proceeding to the end of the book (folding/stacking/fan-like arrangement explains this order).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes possibility that earlier formats may have been written left-to-right and horizontally (roll-like), but current folded form produces the right-to-left top-to-bottom convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters built from elemental strokes / primitive radicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Each character is made of a certain number of distinct strokes, lines or marks (letters/elements/particles); combinations of two, three, four or more yield syllables or primitive radical characters each with its own notion or sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author estimates about 300 of this second (primitive) kind; these primitives are building blocks for more compound characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decompounded (compound) characters fit same square as simple ones
rubrics_metrics.description: Compound characters are formed by crowding two or more primitive elements into the same standardized square such that simple and compound characters occupy identical square size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This feature is a notable singularity of Chinese characters and is likely why characters are often treated as real/ideographic rather than literal if their original pronunciation is lost; it also permits both literal and real interpretations of character origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for pronunciation and syntax (monosyllabic court language and tones)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current court language/pronunciation differs from literal character pronunciation: many monosyllables are used to signify many notions and are differentiated by musical toning/accents (sometimes compound tones). Grammatical distinctions are often omitted (same character for noun/adjective, singular/plural, verb tenses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because syntax and sentence context are important, one often must consider the whole sentence and positional rules (order/position in the square) to determine part of speech and meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method to render characters syllabic/literal (universal-character approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is possible to adapt characters into a literal or syllabic system (e.g., Bishop Wilkins' universal character): single characters correspond to monosyllables and compounds to di-/tri-syllables according to number/order of simple characters in the square.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author suggests a scheme where the number and order of simple marks in the square determine syllabic length, enabling legibility into a spoken language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoke-consuming engine performance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The engine must consume all smoke from any kind of wood, be small and portable, be effectively invisible in the room to the eye and not detectable by the nose even with an open fire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement: fire at place A must be well kindled and tunnel B–D very hot so that air cannot enter the tunnel; smoke/flame is forced inward through burning coals where constituents are dispersed/refined to become inoffensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoke-engine construction specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Device composed of nested hammered-iron hoops ~4–5 inches diameter, standing upright on a trevet with a central fire-place (A) and a hot tunnel (B–D) forcing smoke through a heap of burning coals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If wood is taken out of the fire it smokes until returned; very hot tunnel and well-kindled fire are essential; odours and perfumes are destroyed when the device is at proper temperature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical measurement standard: measure distances relative to ring length and record periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Distances of Saturn's inner satellites are given relative to the apparent length of Saturn's ring; periods of revolution are reported precisely (e.g., first satellite 1 day 21h19m, second 2d17h43m).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record conjunction counts and note how ring obliquity affects apparent latitude/distance; provide numerical epochs (radices) for positions relative to perigee and exact observation times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of long focal-length object glasses and predictive motion rules for discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery and reliable observation of faint/close satellites require very long focal-length object glasses (example: 34–220 feet) and knowledge of the rules of their motion to direct observation to the expected places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observations benefited from lenses by Siguier Campani and others; once motion rules were found, even smaller glasses could detect the satellites by pointing to predicted positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of Kepler-like proportional relationships
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportions between digressions (distances) and between periods of satellites reflect regular ratios (e.g., digression ratio 22:17 and period ratio 244:17), analogous to Kepler's relations among planets and satellites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such proportionality is evidence of harmony/uniformity across planetary systems and is used to compare Saturn's satellites to Jupiter's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Astronomical observation reporting details and uncertainties
rubrics_metrics.description: Record precise local times of immersion/emersion, observational conditions (asperity of moon limb, vapours, clouds), and any measurement difficulties; use timings to deduce physical quantities (e.g., Jupiter's diameter from emersion duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide locations, exact times, and references to lunar maps (Hevelius' divisions) to anchor observations; report uncertainties due to seeing/limb irregularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative tabulation of satellite periods
rubrics_metrics.description: List and compare periods of satellites of different planets side-by-side to reveal analogies (table of periods for Jupiter's and Saturn's satellites).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these comparisons to argue for uniformity among celestial systems and to highlight exceptions (e.g., first Saturn satellite differs from the general shorter-times trend).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis: internal agitation sustains dissolved particles
rubrics_metrics.description: A dissolved heavy substance may remain suspended in a lighter menstruum because internal motion/agitation of the solvent sustains very minute particles despite their specific gravity; heating increases this agitation and solubility, cooling precipitates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the known experimental fact that a hot menstruum dissolves more than a cold one and cooling causes precipitation as supporting evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objection and counterargument regarding precipitation upon mixing liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Precipitation induced by mixing an alkali with an acid challenges the agitation-only explanation since fluidity is not destroyed; counterargument: mixing changes pore conformation and forces insensible parts to aggregate, increasing effective particle size and causing settling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain precipitation as resulting from induced aggregation (clinging together) that makes particles heavier than what internal agitation can sustain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative account: cohesion/congruity of liquid parts resists particle separation
rubrics_metrics.description: Liquids have an innate tendency for parts to unite (congruity) and resist separation; very minute particles of a dissolved solid may not have sufficient weight to overcome this cohesion and therefore remain afloat in a lighter menstruum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relate resistance to surface effects: resistance of medium acts on surface whereas gravity acts on bulk, and as particle size decreases surface-to-volume ratio increases, making resistance comparatively larger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaling argument: surface vs bulk in resisting sinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Resistance from the medium operates in proportion to a body's surface, while gravity is proportional to volume; as bodies are subdivided, surface decreases slower than bulk (surface ∝ diameter^2, volume ∝ diameter^3), so sufficiently small particles experience proportionally larger resistance relative to their weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use analogy to air resistance deviating Galileo's descent proportions and to explain why extremely small dissolved particles may be wholly resisted/sustained by the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for medical case reporting (history, symptoms, outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a chronological history of the patient's condition (dates, symptoms, exacerbations), detailed symptom descriptions (nausea, hiccup, convulsions, stone expulsions), observations of urine and stool behavior, physical signs (tumid abdomen, sounds of calculi), treatments applied, and outcome evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report frequency/timing of calculi expulsion, associated bleeding or gangrene, and any symptomatic patterns (e.g., constipation preceding stone voiding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chemical testing protocol for calculi
rubrics_metrics.description: Test calculi with various reagents and record reactions: spirits of sulphuric/vitriolic/acetique produce effervescence on friable gastric stones but do not fully dissolve; spirit of sal ammoniac shows no action; spirit of nitre (nitric acid) completely dissolves the calculi.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note differences in texture (loose/friable vs harder/angular) and origin (stomach-ejected vs other) when interpreting reagent results; present chemical findings as part of diagnostic/rationale discussion.
